proofs.proof_tex:
Write \(\mathscr X=\sigma\{X_{st}:1\le s\le S,1\le t\le T\}\).  We construct all experiments conditional on a fixed value of \(E_0\).  The query is chosen in a fixed compact subset of the interior of \(([0,1]^d)^S\), and \(\mathcal Z_+\) is chosen to contain that compact set; hence the displayed positive-query probability is one.  Historical coordinates are i.i.d. with a density between the prescribed fixed bounds.  Conditional on \(\mathscr X\), historical responses are independent across units and dates, are supported in \([0,B]\), and have means \(m_s(X_{st})\).  Their Bernoulli probabilities are kept in a fixed subinterval of \((0,1)\), so their conditional variances are bounded below by \(B^{-1}\) after choosing the fixed scale within the nonempty compatibility range of the class constants.  Event outcomes are bounded and independent across units and of \(\mathscr X\).  Unobserved event-date untreated potential outcomes are completed with cohort-average conditional mean \(m_s(z_{0s})\).  Consistency, historical consistency, no spillovers, limited anticipation, and event transport then hold.  Moreover,
\[
\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]
=\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0],
\qquad
\mathbb E_P[Q_{sti}-m_s(X_{st})\mid\mathscr X,E_0]=0.
\]
Thus every construction below satisfies the two defining restrictions of \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\).  Independent calendar coordinates have zero conditional \(\beta\)-mixing coefficients.  The donor variables are independent of the panel, i.i.d. conditional on \(E_0\), and are chosen with covariance eigenvalues in \([c_\Sigma,C_\Sigma]\) and standardized fourth moment at most \(B\).  Exact training coordinates are obtained by setting \(X_{st}^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_{st}\).

We use one elementary Bernoulli bound repeatedly.  If \(p,p+v\in[\eta,1-\eta]\), then Taylor's theorem applied to the Bernoulli relative entropy gives
\[
\operatorname{kl}(p+v,p)
\le \frac{v^2}{2\eta(1-\eta)}.
\tag{1}
\]
Also, for product experiments, direct expansion of the log likelihood ratio gives additivity of Kullback--Leibler divergence.

For the treated channel, put
\[
V_{\mathrm{tr}}=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}
\]
and change the event Bernoulli mean in cohort \(s\) by
\[
v_s=c_0\frac{\pi_s}{n_sV_{\mathrm{tr}}^{1/2}},
\]
where \(c_0>0\) is fixed sufficiently small.  Since \(S\) and the weights are fixed and \(n_s\to\infty\), all probabilities remain in \([\eta,1-\eta]\).  The target separation is
\[
\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_sv_s
=c_0V_{\mathrm{tr}}^{-1/2}\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}
=c_0R_{\mathrm{tr}}^{1/2}.
\tag{2}
\]
By (1), the divergence of all event observations is at most
\[
C\sum_{s=1}^{S}n_sv_s^2=Cc_0^2.
\tag{3}
\]
All other observed variables have the same law.  Taking \(c_0\) small makes the testing affinity uniformly positive.

For the smoothing channel choose \(s_*\) maximizing
\[
\pi_s^2(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}.
\]
Because \(S\) is fixed, this maximum is at least \(R_{\mathrm{sm}}/S\).  Put
\[
b=(Tn_{s_*})^{-1/(2\lambda+d)}
\]
and let \(\psi\) be a fixed compactly supported \(\lambda\)-Holder bump with \(\psi(0)=1\).  Perturb only the \(s_*\)-surface by
\[
m_{s_*,1}(x)-m_{s_*,0}(x)=c_1b^\lambda
\psi\!\left(\frac{x-z_{0s_*}}b\right).
\tag{4}
\]
The constant \(c_1\) is chosen small enough that both surfaces remain in the Holder ball, in the response interior, and within the same two-sided local-modulus bounds; a common affine carrier is used when \(\lambda>1\), and a common one-sided \(\lambda\)-cusp carrier is used when \(0<\lambda\le1\).  These carriers have respectively modulus exponents one and \(\lambda\), hence exponent \(\kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\}\).  Formula (4) gives target separation
\[
c_1\pi_{s_*}b^\lambda,
\qquad
c_1^2\pi_{s_*}^2b^{2\lambda}\ge \frac{c}{S}R_{\mathrm{sm}}.
\tag{5}
\]
Only a set of design probability at most \(Cb^d\) is perturbed.  Applying (1), integrating over the design, and summing over \(Tn_{s_*}\) responses gives
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_{1,\mathrm{sm}},P_{0,\mathrm{sm}})
\le C Tn_{s_*}b^{2\lambda+d}=C.
\tag{6}
\]

For the spacing channel take \(h=c_2T^{-1/d}\) and use the same local perturbation as in (4), now with bandwidth \(h\), in any fixed cohort with positive weight.  Choose its support ball \(A_h\) so that \(P(X_{st}\in A_h\mid E_0)\le Cc_2^d/T\).  On
\[
\mathcal A_h=\{X_{st}\notin A_h\text{ for every }t\},
\]
the complete observed conditional response kernels under the two laws coincide.  Independence of the calendar coordinates yields
\[
P(\mathcal A_h\mid E_0)
\ge\left(1-\frac{Cc_2^d}{T}\right)^T
\ge c'>0
\tag{7}
\]
for sufficiently small fixed \(c_2\).  Hence the overlap integral of the two joint laws is at least \(c'\).  Their target separation is a fixed positive multiple of
\[
h^\lambda=T^{-\lambda/d},
\tag{8}
\]
whose square is \(R_{\mathrm{sp}}\).  This argument uses the no-design-point event and asserts no bounded Kullback--Leibler divergence.

For the donor channel take a globally affine carrier when \(\lambda>1\), and a globally defined asymmetric \(\lambda\)-cusp carrier when \(0<\lambda\le1\).  Scale it so that its covariance-standardized weighted modulus lies between \(c_{\mathrm{mod}}\delta^\kappa\) and \(C_{\mathrm{mod}}\delta^\kappa\) throughout the declared interior radius.  There is then a covariance-standardized direction \(u_N\) with
\[
\|\Sigma^{-1/2}u_N\|_2=c_3N^{-1/2}le\delta_0
\]
and
\[
\left|\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
\{m_s(z_{0s}+u_{N,s})-m_s(z_{0s})\}\right|
\ge cN^{-\kappa/2}.
\tag{9}
\]
Under the two laws let the donor observations have a common bounded, smooth location-family density with covariance \(\Sigma\), means respectively \(z_0\) and \(z_0+u_N\), and finite standardized fourth moment within the declared envelope.  Choosing the fixed location family with finite Fisher information and expanding its log density, or directly using a Gaussian carrier when the fourth-moment envelope permits it, gives
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_{1,\mathrm{don}},P_{0,\mathrm{don}})
\le CN\|\Sigma^{-1/2}u_N\|_2^2
=Cc_3^2.
\tag{10}
\]
Keep the observed event mean fixed and complete the unobserved untreated event outcome under each law with mean \(m_s(z_{0s})\).  The identifying formula then makes (9) exactly the target separation, whose square is at least \(cN^{-\kappa}=cR_{\mathrm{don}}\).

For the three bounded-divergence experiments, let \(A=\{dP_1/dP_0\ge1\}\), put \(p=P_1(A)\), and put \(q=P_0(A)\).  The log-sum inequality, obtained by applying Jensen's inequality separately on \(A\) and \(A^c\), gives
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_1,P_0)
\ge p\log\frac pq+(1-p)\log\frac{1-p}{1-q}
\ge2(p-q)^2,
\]
where the final inequality follows by differentiating the binary relative entropy twice in \(p\).  Since \(p-q=\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\) and \(\int\min(dP_0,dP_1)=1-\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\),
\[
\int\min(dP_0,dP_1)
\ge1-\sqrt{\operatorname{KL}(P_1,P_0)/2}.
\]
The perturbation constants in (2), (4), and (9) can be reduced so that the right-hand side is a fixed positive number.  Equation (7) supplies the corresponding affinity directly for spacing.  The causal completions preceding (1) verify all panel-law conditions, including the two full-design restrictions, and complete the proof.

Fix an estimator \(\widetilde\tau\) and a channel \(q\).  Apply \texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding} to obtain two laws in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\) with target values \(\theta_0,\theta_1\), separation \(\Delta_q=|\theta_1-\theta_0|\ge cR_q^{1/2}\), and affinity \(A_q=\int\min(dP_{0,q},dP_{1,q})\ge a_0>0\).  The events
\[
E_0'=\{|\widetilde\tau-\theta_0|\ge\Delta_q/2\},
\qquad
E_1'=\{|\widetilde\tau-\theta_1|\ge\Delta_q/2\}
\]
cover the sample space pointwise, because their complements would imply \(|\theta_1-\theta_0|<\Delta_q\).  Therefore
\[
P_{0,q}(E_0')+P_{1,q}(E_1')
\ge\int\min(dP_{0,q},dP_{1,q})
\ge a_0.
\]
Markov's inequality in reverse on each error event gives
\[
\max_{\ell\in\{0,1\}}
\mathbb E_{P_{\ell,q}}[(\widetilde\tau-\theta_\ell)^2\mid E_0]
\ge\frac{\Delta_q^2}{8}a_0
\ge cR_q.
\]
Taking the supremum over the subclass, then the infimum over estimators, and finally the maximum over the four channels yields
\[
\inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)}
\mathbb E_P[(\widetilde\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0]
\ge c\max_qR_q=cR_\star.
\]
The omitted upper bound is not a proof gap: \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-spacing-obstruction} gives laws in this same subclass whose minimax risk is of order at least \((\log T/T)^2\) when the frozen benchmark is \(R_\star=T^{-2}\).

Let \(\mathscr X=\sigma\{X_{st}:s\le S,t\le T\}\), and condition first on \((\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)_{j=1}^{N})\).  On a successful fit, polynomial reproduction gives
\[
\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}a_{stik}
p(u_{stk})=p(0)
\]
for every polynomial \(p\) of total degree at most \(r\).  Applying this identity to the Taylor polynomial of \(m_s\) at \(\widetilde z_{sk}\), and then applying the Holder remainder bound, yields
\[
\left|e_0^\top\widehat\gamma_{sk}
-m_s(\widetilde z_{sk})
-\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}a_{stik}\varepsilon_{sti}\right|
\le C_{r,d}L\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}
|a_{stik}|\|X_{st}-\widetilde z_{sk}\|_2^\lambda.
\tag{11}
\]
After weighting and averaging folds, the right-hand side is \(A_L\).

By \texttt{ass:historical-full-design-centering}, the random variables
\[
U_{si}=\pi_s\sum_{t=1}^{T}\bar a_{sti}\varepsilon_{sti}
\]
have conditional mean zero.  By conditional cross-unit independence they are conditionally independent over \((s,i)\), and their conditional range lengths are at most
\[
B\pi_s\sum_{t=1}^{T}|\bar a_{sti}|.
\]
For a centered random variable with range length \(c\), convexity of the exponential and optimization over the two endpoint distribution imply
\[
\mathbb E[e^{vU}\mid\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)]\le e^{v^2c^2/8}.
\]
Multiplying these bounds over units and applying Chernoff's inequality at the optimizing \(v\) gives
\[
P\!\left(\left|\sum_{s,i}U_{si}\right|>R_{\mathrm{hist}}
\,\middle|\,\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)\right)
\le\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}}.
\tag{12}
\]

Likewise, \texttt{ass:event-full-design-mean-stability} centers
\[
V_{si}=\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}
\left(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0]\right)
\]
conditional on \(\mathscr X,E_0\).  These variables are conditionally independent over units and have range lengths at most \(B\pi_s/n_s\).  The same calculation yields
\[
P\!\left(\left|\sum_{s,i}V_{si}\right|>R_{\mathrm{evt}}
\,\middle|\,\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)\right)
\le\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}}.
\tag{13}
\]
No independence between a given unit's event and historical outcomes is used: (12) and (13) are combined only by a union bound.

It remains to calibrate the generated center.  Conditional donor replication gives independent vectors
\[
Y_j=\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0),
\qquad
\mathbb E[Y_j\mid E_0]=0,
\qquad
\mathbb E[Y_jY_j^\top\mid E_0]=I_D.
\]
Expanding the fourth power and using independence shows, for a complement of size \(m=m_k\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E\left\|m^{-1/2}\sum_{j\notin k}Y_j\right\|_2^4
&=m^{-1}\mathbb E\|Y_1\|_2^4
+\left(1-\frac1m\right)
\left\{(\operatorname{tr}I_D)^2+2\operatorname{tr}(I_D^2)\right\}\\
&\le \frac Bm+\left(1-\frac1m\right)(D^2+2D)
=M_4(m).
\end{aligned}
\tag{14}
\]
Markov's inequality at \(q_k\), followed by a union bound over \(k\), gives total conditional error at most \(\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}\).  Euclidean projection onto the cube is nonexpansive.  The eigenvalue bounds on \(\Sigma\) therefore imply, on the complementary-fold event,
\[
\left\|\Sigma^{-1/2}
\left(\operatorname{vec}((\widetilde z_{sk})_{s=1}^{S})-z_0\right)\right\|_2
\le\delta_k.
\tag{15}
\]
When \(\delta_k\le\delta_0\), the upper half of the local-modulus assumption and (15) give
\[
\left|\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
\{m_s(\widetilde z_{sk})-m_s(z_{0s})\}\right|
\le C_{\mathrm{mod}}\delta_k^\kappa.
\]
Averaging folds bounds the generated-center discrepancy by \(A_{\mathrm{don}}\).

Using \texttt{lem:identification-fwl}, decompose \(\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0)\) into the event sum in (13), the negative historical sum in (12), the Taylor remainder in (11), and the generated-center discrepancy.  With conditional probability at least
\[
1-\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}}-\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}}-\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}=1-\alpha,
\]
its absolute value is at most \(H_\alpha\).  On every declared bad sample, \(C_\alpha=[-B,B]\), while \(\tau_n(z_0)\in[-B,B]\) by bounded event wealth.  This proves the displayed uniform conditional coverage.

For the expected-length lower bound, reduce the perturbation constants in \texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding}, if necessary, so every channel affinity \(A_q\) exceeds \(2\alpha+a_0\) for a fixed \(a_0>0\).  If an interval \(C\) covers both target values with error at most \(\alpha\), then
\[
P_{0,q}\{\theta_0,\theta_1\in C\}
\ge A_q-2\alpha\ge a_0.
\]
Indeed, integrate the indicator of the intersection against \(P_{0,q}\wedge P_{1,q}\) and use the two coverage failures.  On that intersection, \(\operatorname{length}(C)\ge\Delta_q\), hence
\[
\max_{\ell\in\{0,1\}}
\mathbb E_{P_{\ell,q}}[\operatorname{length}(C)\mid E_0]
\ge c\Delta_q\ge cR_q^{1/2}.
\]
Maximizing over \(q\) proves the \(cR_\star^{1/2}\) lower bound.  The excluded upper bound is false by \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-spacing-obstruction}.

added_lemmas.statement:
On every successful normalized-shape fit,
\[
\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}|a_{stik}|
\le\{L_{sk}e_0^\top G_{sk}^{-1}e_0\}^{1/2}
\le c_G^{-1/2}.
\]
Because weights and covariates do not depend on the replicated-unit index,
\[
\sum_t|a_{stik}|\le \frac{c_G^{-1/2}}{n_s},
\qquad
\sum_t|\bar a_{sti}|\le \frac{c_G^{-1/2}}{n_s},
\]
and consequently
\[
\sum_{s=1}^{S}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}
\left[\pi_s\sum_t|\bar a_{sti}|\right]^2
\le c_G^{-1}R_{\mathrm{tr}}.
\]
The exact Taylor bias is bounded by \(A_L\).  These deterministic conclusions require no upper local-mass event.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Suppress \((s,k)\), write \(\mathsf L=L_{sk}\), and write \(v_{ti}=w_{stk}^{1/2}b_r(u_{stk})\).  Since
\[
G=\sum_{t,i}v_{ti}v_{ti}^\top,
\qquad
a_{ti}=w_{stk}^{1/2}e_0^\top G^{-1}v_{ti},
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{t,i}|a_{ti}|
&\le
\left\{\sum_{t,i}(e_0^\top G^{-1}v_{ti})^2\right\}^{1/2}
\left\{\sum_{t,i}w_{stk}\right\}^{1/2}\\
&=\{e_0^\top G^{-1}GG^{-1}e_0\}^{1/2}\mathsf L^{1/2}
=\{\mathsf Le_0^\top G^{-1}e_0\}^{1/2}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The selector's shape inequality is \(G/\mathsf L\succeq c_GI\), so \(G^{-1}\preceq(c_G\mathsf L)^{-1}I\).  Because \(e_0=b_r(0)\) is the constant-monomial coordinate and has Euclidean norm one under the declared monomial basis,
\[
\mathsf Le_0^\top G^{-1}e_0\le c_G^{-1}.
\]
For fixed \((s,t,k)\), neither \(w_{stk}\) nor \(u_{stk}\) depends on \(i\), while \(G=n_s\sum_tw_{stk}b_r(u_{stk})b_r(u_{stk})^\top\).  Thus \(a_{stik}\) is the same for every \(i\), and
\[
n_s\sum_t|a_{stik}|=\sum_{t,i}|a_{stik}|\le c_G^{-1/2}.
\]
The triangle inequality after averaging the fixed number of folds gives the same bound for \(\bar a_{sti}\).  Therefore
\[
\sum_{s,i}\left[\pi_s\sum_t|\bar a_{sti}|\right]^2
\le\sum_sn_s\left(\frac{\pi_sc_G^{-1/2}}{n_s}\right)^2
=c_G^{-1}\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}
=c_G^{-1}R_{\mathrm{tr}}.
\]
Finally, the normal equations reproduce every polynomial of degree at most \(r\).  Subtracting the degree-\(r\) Taylor polynomial of \(m_s\) at \(\widetilde z_{sk}\), applying the Holder remainder
\[
|m_s(x)-T_{r,\widetilde z_{sk}}m_s(x)|
\le C_{r,d}L\|x-\widetilde z_{sk}\|_2^\lambda,
\]
and summing absolute weighted remainders gives exactly the displayed definition of \(A_L\).  No bound on \(L_{sk}\) from above was used.

added_lemmas.statement:
There is an admissible fixed choice of class constants with \(S=d=p=1\), \(H=0\), \(\lambda=\kappa=1\), and a triangular array of pairs
\[
(P_{0,T},P_{1,T})\subset\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}^{\dagger}(1),
\qquad n_1=N=T^4,
\]
whose observed-data affinity is bounded away from zero and whose targets differ by \(c\log(T)/T\).  Consequently,
\[
\inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}^{\dagger}(1)}
\mathbb E_P[(\widetilde\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0]
\ge c\frac{\log^2T}{T^2},
\]
and every uniformly conditionally \((1-\alpha)\)-honest interval has worst-case expected length at least \(c_\alpha\log(T)/T\), although the frozen benchmark is \(R_\star=T^{-2}\).  Thus uniform marginal design-density bounds and geometric \(\beta\)-mixing alone do not imply the no-log normalized-shape selector moment bound or either asserted \(R_\star\) upper frontier.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Take \(B=16\), \(c_X=C_X=1\), \(z_0=1/2\), \(\delta_0=1/4\), and fixed modulus constants satisfying
\[
0<c_{\mathrm{mod}}<A-\gamma<A<C_{\mathrm{mod}}
\]
for fixed \(A,\gamma>0\); take \(L>A+\gamma\).  Let \(E_0\) be constant and \(\mathcal Z_+=\{z_0\}\).  Put
\[
L_T=\left\lfloor\frac{\log T}{2|\log\rho_0|}\right\rfloor\vee1,
\qquad
p_T=\frac{L_T}{4T},
\qquad
h_T=\frac{p_T}{2},
\qquad
A_T=[z_0-h_T,z_0+h_T].
\]
Partition \(\{1,\ldots,T\}\) into deterministic consecutive blocks of length \(L_T\), apart from a final shorter block.  Independently over blocks draw \(G_b\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_T)\).  Conditional on \(G_b=1\), draw every \(X_t\) in block \(b\) independently and uniformly on \(A_T\); conditional on \(G_b=0\), draw them independently and uniformly on \([0,1]\setminus A_T\).  For each \(t\),
\[
p_T\frac{\mathbf1_{A_T}(x)}{p_T}
+(1-p_T)\frac{\mathbf1_{[0,1]\setminus A_T}(x)}{1-p_T}=1,
\]
so every marginal design density is exactly uniform.

If two calendar sigma-fields at separation \(k\) do not meet the same deterministic block, they are independent.  If they do meet one block, their only shared variable is the Bernoulli label \(G_b\).  The absolute-regularity coefficient of two copies of that label is at most \(2p_T(1-p_T)\le2p_T\).  Hence
\[
\beta_P(k\mid E_0)\le
\begin{cases}
2p_T,&1\le k<L_T,\\
0,&k\ge L_T.
\end{cases}
\]
For \(k<L_T\), the smallest right side in the desired geometric envelope occurs at \(k=L_T-1\), and
\[
\beta_0\rho_0^{L_T-1}\ge cT^{-1/2}
\ge \frac{L_T}{2T}=2p_T
\]
for all sufficiently large \(T\).  Thus the frozen geometric mixing condition holds with the fixed \((\beta_0,\rho_0)\).

Define two regression surfaces by
\[
m_0(x)=4+A|x-z_0|,
\qquad
m_1(x)=m_0(x)+\gamma(h_T-|x-z_0|)_+.
\tag{16}
\]
They agree off \(A_T\), take values in a fixed compact subinterval of \((0,8)\), and are in the fixed Lipschitz ball.  For \(0<\delta\le h_T\),
\[
\omega_{P_0}(\delta;z_0)=A\delta,
\qquad
\omega_{P_1}(\delta;z_0)=(A-\gamma)\delta.
\]
For \(h_T<\delta\le\delta_0\), evaluating at \(|u|=\delta\) and using (16) gives
\[
(A-\gamma)\delta
\le A\delta-\gamma h_T
\le\omega_{P_1}(\delta;z_0)
\le A\delta.
\]
Thus both laws satisfy the same two-sided local modulus with exponent \(\kappa=1\).

Under law \(P_\ell\), conditional on the complete design, draw the \(Q_{ti}\) independently over \((t,i)\) with
\[
Q_{ti}=8V_{ti},
\qquad
V_{ti}\mid\mathscr X,E_0\sim
\operatorname{Bernoulli}\{m_\ell(X_t)/8\}.
\]
Here \(\mathscr X=\sigma(X_1,\ldots,X_T)\).
Then \(0\le Q_{ti}\le8<B\), its full-design conditional mean is \(m_\ell(X_t)\), and its conditional variance is bounded below by a fixed constant greater than \(B^{-1}\).  The historical errors are centered conditional on the complete design, and unit histories are conditionally independent.  Set \(B_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_i(1)=8\) deterministically and complete \(B_i(0)\in[0,8]\) independently with mean \(m_\ell(z_0)\).  Event transport holds, event means are stable given the full design, and the causal target is
\[
\tau_{n,P_\ell}(z_0)=8-m_\ell(z_0).
\]
All historical potential outcomes are set equal across path-status labels, which verifies limited anticipation and historical consistency; consistency and no spillovers are immediate.

Let donors be \(Z_j=z_0+U_j\), where the \(U_j\) are independent Rademacher variables independent of the panel.  Then \(\Sigma=1\), the standardized fourth moment is one, and all donor conditions hold.  Set \(X_t^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_t\).  These calculations verify that both complete causal laws belong to \(\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}^{\dagger}(1)\).

The event
\[
\mathcal A_T=\{G_b=0\text{ for every block }b\}
\]
contains no historical design point in \(A_T\).  Since the two regression surfaces agree outside \(A_T\), the entire observed-data conditional kernels agree on \(\mathcal A_T\).  Moreover,
\[
P(\mathcal A_T\mid E_0)
=(1-p_T)^{\lceil T/L_T\rceil}
\longrightarrow e^{-1/4}.
\]
It follows directly by integrating the common conditional density over \(\mathcal A_T\) that
\[
\int\min(dP_{0,T},dP_{1,T})\ge P(\mathcal A_T\mid E_0)\ge c>0.
\]
But (16) yields
\[
|\tau_{n,P_1}(z_0)-\tau_{n,P_0}(z_0)|
=|m_1(z_0)-m_0(z_0)|
=\gamma h_T\asymp\frac{\log T}{T}.
\]
For any estimator, the two error events at radius one half of this separation cover the sample space; integration against the common part \(P_{0,T}\wedge P_{1,T}\) therefore gives squared risk at least a fixed multiple of \(h_T^2\).  For any interval having coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) under both laws, reduction of \(p_T\), if needed, makes the limiting affinity exceed \(2\alpha\); integrating the simultaneous-coverage event against the common part gives expected length at least a fixed positive multiple of \(h_T\).  These are the asserted risk and length lower bounds.

Finally, with \(n_1=N=T^4\) and \(d=\lambda=\kappa=1\),
\[
R_{\mathrm{tr}}=T^{-4},\qquad
R_{\mathrm{sm}}=(T^5)^{-2/3}=T^{-10/3},\qquad
R_{\mathrm{sp}}=T^{-2},\qquad
R_{\mathrm{don}}=T^{-4},
\]
and hence \(R_\star=T^{-2}\).  The ratio of the actual lower bound to \(R_\star\) diverges as \(\log^2T\).  The construction is not a large-local-mass pathology: it is a legal rare-state clustering process allowed by a marginal density bound and geometric absolute regularity.  A sequential conditional small-ball condition, such as \texttt{ass:sequential-design-overlap}, excludes it; the frozen assumptions do not.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:

\[
u_{stk}(h)=\frac{X_{st}-\widetilde z_{sk}}{h},\qquad
w_{stk}(h)=K(u_{stk}(h)),
\]
\[
L_{sk}(h)=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}w_{stk}(h),\qquad
G_{sk}(h)=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}w_{stk}(h)b_r(u_{stk}(h))b_r(u_{stk}(h))^{\top}.
\]
Let \(c_G>0\) be the fixed procedural shape constant determined by the kernel, polynomial basis, design-density bounds, and interior constant.  On the finite dyadic grid starting at \(h_s\) and ending at \(1\), select the first \(h=h_{sk}\) such that
\[
L_{sk}(h)>0,
\qquad
\lambda_{\min}\!\left\{G_{sk}(h)/L_{sk}(h)\right\}\ge c_G.
\]
If no grid value passes, declare the fit failed.  On a successful fit set \(u_{stk}=u_{stk}(h_{sk})\), \(w_{stk}=w_{stk}(h_{sk})\), and let \(\widehat\gamma_{sk}\) minimize
\[
\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}w_{stk}
\left[Q_{sti}-b_r(u_{stk})^{\top}\gamma\right]^2.
\]
Define
\[
\widehat m_s=K_D^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^{K_D}e_0^{\top}\widehat\gamma_{sk},
\qquad
\widehat\tau=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
\left(\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}-\widehat m_s\right).
\]
On a failed selected fit set its intercept contribution to zero.  Estimate \(\Sigma\) by the spectrally clipped full sample covariance \(\widehat\Sigma\); no clipping is applied to a successful fitted intercept or to \(\widehat\tau\).

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:

\[

\qquad
a_{stik}=e_0^{\top}G_{sk}^{-1}w_{stk}b_r(u_{stk}),
\]
\[

\qquad
\widehat m_s=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\bar a_{sti}Q_{sti}.
\]
Set
\[
A_L=C_{r,d}L\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s}{K_D}
\sum_{k=1}^{K_D}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}

\[

prose_updates.tldr: The target is the cohort-weighted finite-cohort causal buy-and-hold level-wealth effect at a realized event path. Maintained cohort-average event transport identifies it through the full historical wealth-path regression, and the raw generated-center local-polynomial estimator remains exactly the event coefficient of the weighted panel regression. On the subclass imposing two explicit strong full-design strict-exogeneity and centering restrictions, a full-data interval using exact Hoeffding radii, an observable Holder allowance, and a full-covariance donor allowance is uniformly conditionally honest. Four joint causal-panel experiments prove the treated, smoothing, spacing, and donor lower benchmarks. A new rare-state block witness shows, however, that marginal design density plus geometric beta mixing permits a log(T)/T spacing scale, so neither the R-star risk upper bound nor the R-star square-root expected-length upper bound is valid on that subclass without an additional sequential local-overlap condition.

project_justification.gap: Existing repeated-measurement, generated-regressor, and synthetic-control results do not jointly distinguish causal identification, full-design replication, generated event centers, and local-design anti-clustering. In particular, geometric beta mixing and a marginal density bound do not by themselves yield iid-quality pointwise spacing.
project_justification.niche: The panel architecture observes historical proxy paths exactly, replicates bounded wealth blocks across units, and generates only the event-date query from an independent donor universe. This makes it possible to isolate which conclusions follow from causal transport and full-design centering and which additionally require sequential local overlap.
project_justification.fill: The note supplies the identifying functional and exact FWL representation, embeds all four lower-bound channels in full-design-centered causal panels, gives an exact full-data bias-aware conditionally honest interval, and proves an explicit geometrically mixing obstruction to the advertised no-log upper frontier. It also states a primitive sequential conditional-density condition that would exclude the obstruction rather than hiding the missing premise in a selector success event.

sampling_model.design: Conditional on the event state \(E_0\), each cohort has \(T\) exactly observed pre-event proxy paths with one-time densities bounded above and away from zero and a geometrically beta-mixing calendar process. These conditions permit rare local-state clustering; sequential conditional-density overlap is proposed separately and is not treated as a consequence of mixing.
sampling_model.units: At each historical path, cohort \(s\) supplies \(n_s\) conditionally independent bounded untreated wealth blocks. On the restricted class, historical errors are explicitly centered given the complete design and event means are explicitly stable given that design; these are strong added restrictions, not consequences of ordinary cross-unit independence or contemporaneous regression centering.
sampling_model.treatment: The event occurs at \(t=0\). Consistency, limited anticipation, no spillovers, and the maintained cross-date cohort-average event-transport equality identify the untreated finite-cohort event mean from the historical path regression.
sampling_model.overlap: The realized event path lies in an interior positive-probability region and every one-time historical design density is bounded below there. This marginal overlap does not guarantee iid-quality calendar spacing under the allowed triangular beta-mixing laws.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: An independent conditional donor sample estimates only the event query and its unknown full covariance. The repaired local-polynomial selector tests normalized Gram shape. The honest interval uses the full-data raw estimator, exact bounded-unit-history and bounded-event Hoeffding radii, the exact observable Taylor allowance, and a fourth-moment full-covariance donor radius; it uses no retained-block jackknife, multiplier law, or dense-local-site condition.

prose_updates.related_work: Goldsmith-Pinkham and Lyu motivate the causal financial-panel and volatility-drag layers; their work does not replace the maintained event-transport restriction. Yan, Yao, and Zhou study repeated-measurement prediction, Gaiffas studies pointwise random-design smoothing, and Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle study generated coordinates attached to training observations. Delaigle, Hall, and Meister concern replicated classical measurement error and deconvolution, which is absent because historical paths are exact. Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik motivate conditional synthetic-control uncertainty and mixing arguments, but geometric beta mixing alone does not preclude the rare-state clustering constructed here. Armstrong and Kolesar motivate modulus-based honest-length comparisons. The present proved contribution is the joint causal-panel embedding, exact FWL identity, full-data conditional coverage construction, and explicit separation between a four-channel lower benchmark and the stronger sequential-overlap premise needed for a no-log upper frontier.
prose_updates.interpretation: Full-design centering repairs the shared-design replication failure but not the local-spacing failure. More donor securities reduce the generated-center term and more replicated units reduce bounded unit-history and event fluctuations; neither remedy creates new calendar locations near a realized query. Under the frozen dependence class, calendar locations may arrive in rare blocks, making the effective local-spacing scale log(T)/T in the exhibited scalar array.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Causal identification remains conditional on cohort-average event transport. The donor lower channel remains conditional on the assumed two-sided local modulus, which excludes flat surfaces. Sharp risk and honest-length statements are explicitly restricted to the subclass with event full-design mean stability and historical full-design centering.
